name: Etam
overview: Etam was a male member of the tribe of Judah, noted primarily as the father of Jezreel, Ishma, Ibdash, and Hazzelelponi. His mention is brief and centers on his role within this familial context. There are no additional notes or details about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Etam is a proper name and is possibly derived from a term meaning 'birds of prey.' This meaning may reflect a characteristic or symbolic aspect of the name, though the Scripture does not elaborate on this significance.
familyAndRelationships: Etam is recorded as the father of four children: Jezreel, Ishma, Ibdash, and Hazzelelponi. Beyond these relationships, Scripture does not provide further family details about him.
scriptureSignificance: Etam's significance lies in his genealogical role within the tribe of Judah, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:3. His mention serves to trace the lineage and heritage important to the biblical narrative of the people of Israel. While brief, this reference contributes to the broader understanding of tribal connections and family lines in the Old Testament.
